NoteTexAccessor::sections¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch NoteTexAccessor::sections() const

Extract Top-Level Section Titles¶

sections() extracts the required title body from every complete \section or \section* call. It accepts an optional short title before the required body, but returns the authored long title because that is the content attached to the document section. Nested braces inside the title are retained.

This method targets exactly one structural depth. It does not include \subsection, \subsubsection, \chapter, or longer command names such as \sectional. Use headings(max_depth) for a combined outline through several depths. Escaped commands and incomplete optional or required groups produce no token; source text is never repaired or modified.

The result is a closed TokenBatch. tokens() is a flat Text Note in source order. offsets() is an Int64 Note of length receiver.numel() + 1; the titles for flattened cell i occupy tokens()[offsets[i] ... offsets[i + 1]). Thus a matrix receiver remains recoverable lane by lane even though the number of titles differs per cell. The token Note itself is always rank one.

No matches produce a defined empty Text token Note and zero-valued offsets. An undefined receiver produces undefined tokens and the canonical offsets [0]. Defined non-Text input rejects. Extraction is non-mutating, scans every cell once, and allocates only the flattened title bytes and cumulative offsets.

Example 1: Stars, Optional Titles, Nested Braces, And Boundaries¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\section[Short]{A {nested} title} \section*{Second})",
    R"(\\section{escaped} \sectional{long} \section{unfinished)",
    "plain"});
const auto batch = source.tex().sections();
std::cout << batch.tokens() << '\n';
const auto offsets = batch.offsets().integers();
std::cout << "offsets=[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["A {nested} title", "Second"]
offsets=[0, 2, 2, 2]

Both titles belong to the first input cell. The remaining cells contribute equal adjacent offsets and therefore empty token slices.

Example 2: Recovering Ownership From A Matrix¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\section{A})", "plain",
                             R"(\section{B}\section{C})", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto batch = grid.tex().sections();
std::cout << batch.tokens() << '\n';
const auto offsets = batch.offsets().integers();
std::cout << "offsets=[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A", "B", "C"]
offsets=[0, 1, 1, 3, 3]

Flattened matrix cell 2 owns token positions [1, 3), namely B and C.

Example 3: A Defined Input With No Sections¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"plain", ""}).tex().sections();
std::cout << batch.tokens() << '\n';
const auto offsets = batch.offsets().integers();
std::cout << "offsets=[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]
offsets=[0, 0, 0]

Example 4: Undefined State And Dtype¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().sections();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "tokens defined=" << absent.tokens().defined()
          << " offsets=" << absent.offsets().int_item() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().sections();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "sections Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

tokens defined=false offsets=0
sections Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • headings: extract a combined outline through a chosen depth.

  • subsections: extract only second-level titles.

  • subsubsections: extract only third-level titles.
